findings.summary: A sixth live-verified defect found by N70's real production unit run: `SourceRetriever.fetch` (egress.py, N20-owned, N30 read-only) has a keyword-only `authorization_receipt`/`data_class` contract, but its one production caller -- `D06B_RETRIEVE_SOURCE_CANDIDATES` (runtime/langgraph_factory/nodes/sources.py) -- called it as `fetch(locator, authorization, requests[request_key].get('scope'))`, three positional arguments against a signature that accepts exactly one. Every real discovered locator retrieval therefore raised 'SourceRetriever.fetch() takes 2 positional arguments but 4 were given' unconditionally, live-verified against the real N70 production run for unit L01 (request safety_focus:002's discovery locator). The third argument, `scope` (a fact-category tag like 'applications', not a legitimate `data_class` value -- confirmed by scanning every existing call site and test, none of which ever overrides `data_class` from its 'primary_source_bytes' default), was never a valid parameter for this call at all. Root-caused via direct SQLite checkpoint archaeology of the live run's `writes` table, which showed two concurrent superstep tasks -- D91's own correct repair-classification, and a SEPARATE, independent `_boundary`-caught exception from D06B_RETRIEVE_SOURCE_CANDIDATES racing to the same terminal writer -- exposing this as the true, second, independent root cause behind N70's repeated 'terminal candidate is not a JSON object' symptom (the first being N40V7-F12, filed alongside this finding). Fixed the one call site: `fetch(locator, authorization_receipt=authorization)`, dropping the invalid third argument entirely; egress.py's own signature is correct and untouched. `nodes/sources.py` was not previously covered by any node's write set in this remediation graph -- amended N30_PREFLIGHT_EGRESS's `writes:` list in implementation.graph.v7.yaml to add it (egress/retrieval is squarely this node's domain: N30 already owns the co-located `nodes/inputs.py` and the shared `test_plan26_deterministic_nodes.py`, and already reads `egress.py`), and widened this node's `test_plan26_deterministic_nodes.py` verification filter from 'D03 or capability' to 'D03 or capability or D06B' to cover the new regression test. One prior test double in this same file (`fetch=lambda locator, authorization, scope: ...`) independently encoded the identical wrong calling convention and never caught the bug because it accepted any shape; replaced with the real keyword-only signature, and added a new dedicated regression test (`test_D06B_calls_the_real_source_retriever_fetch_signature`) using a fetch stub that enforces the real signature exactly, proving D06B's call succeeds end-to-end (real `retrievals` entry produced, no `pending_failure`). Full N30 suite: 62 passed/27 subtests (cli/run_curriculum), 16 passed (D03/capability/D06B, up from 10), zero scan violations (6 files now scanned, up from 5), live driver_capabilities.ready: true for both drivers.
